findings.problem: The proof that the decomposition map kills `I` is written twice. It appears in `gradedDecomposePre_vanishes` (lines 104-113) and again inline as the `QuotientAddGroup.lift` argument in `gradedDecompose` (lines 119-127). Both copies use the same steps: `mem_ker`, then `DirectSum.ext`, `Subtype.ext`, the `change` to `mk I (proj i x) = 0`, `eq_zero_iff_mem`, and `hI.mem_iff`. The private lemma exists only so that `gradedDecompose_eq_privateConstruction` can restate the definition by `rfl`. A change to the vanishing argument must therefore be made in two places, and the `rfl` lemma would not detect a mismatch before compilation.
findings.proposed_change: Make the vanishing lemma public by dropping `private`: `theorem gradedDecomposePre_vanishes (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜) : (I : Submodule A A).toAddSubgroup ≤ (gradedDecomposePre 𝒜 I).ker`. Keep the proof at lines 105-113. Then write `gradedDecompose hI := QuotientAddGroup.lift (I : Submodule A A).toAddSubgroup (gradedDecomposePre 𝒜 I) (gradedDecomposePre_vanishes 𝒜 I hI)`. Delete the inline copy and `gradedDecompose_eq_privateConstruction`. `gradedDecompose_mk` already proves `QuotientAddGroup.lift_mk _ _ x`, so it is unaffected. The hypotheses and imports are unchanged. The lemma needs `[DecidableEq ι] [AddMonoid ι] [GradedRing 𝒜]` because `gradedDecomposePre` uses `decomposeAddEquiv`, and it is stated under the same variables as the current private lemma.
findings.benefit: The vanishing proof has a single source and the roughly 10-line duplicate disappears. The private `rfl` bridge lemma is no longer needed. The definition of `gradedDecompose` shows at a glance that it lifts `gradedDecomposePre`.
